candidates.label: NOTE: this problem's stored statementMd is the k-th-shortest-walk problem (not the 'first love' romance title suggests -- a known pre-existing slug/title mismatch, out of scope here). Modified Dijkstra: a min-heap pop finalizes one occurrence of a node's distance; each node may be finalized up to k times (walks may revisit vertices/edges, not simple paths). Answer is the walk-length the k-th finalization of the target y produces, or -1 if fewer than k exist. Hand-verified against the worked example in the statement itself (pentagon graph, x=5,y=2,k=5 -> 15) via the given sample's second case.
Skip condition is cnt[u]>k instead of cnt[u]>=k, so every node is allowed one extra finalization before being cut off -- shifts which walk is reported as the k-th.
Ignores k entirely and computes plain single-source shortest path to y (as if k were always 1) -- wrong whenever k>1 and multiple distinct-length walks exist.
